"9c7d00a7-9e77-5fba-9fff-3a5de26e8749" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \tan{\left(4 x \right)} \sec{\left(4 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "9c7d00a7-9e77-5fba-9fff-3a5de26e8749" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=4 x$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4.
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \tan{\left(4 x \right)} \sec{\left(4 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \tan{\left(u \right)} \sec{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \tan{\left(u \right)} \sec{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=\sec{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Integrate with respect to $u$:

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \tan{\left(u \right)} \sec{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{\sec{\left(u \right)}}{4}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{\sec{\left(4 x \right)}}{4}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "9c7d00a7-9e77-5fba-9fff-3a5de26e8749" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "9c7d00a7-9e77-5fba-9fff-3a5de26e8749" :question/answer-fields \int 2 \cot{\left(3 x \right)} \csc{\left(3 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "7aeb4901-b34d-5d81-a7cc-78f1b155f72f" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=3 x$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=3.
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 2 \cot{\left(3 x \right)} \csc{\left(3 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{2}{3}\left(\int \cot{\left(u \right)} \csc{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \cot{\left(u \right)} \csc{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=- \csc{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Integrate with respect to $u$:

$$
\frac{2}{3}\left(\int \cot{\left(u \right)} \csc{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=- \frac{2 \csc{\left(u \right)}}{3}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
- \frac{2 \csc{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "7aeb4901-b34d-5d81-a7cc-78f1b155f72f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "7aeb4901-b34d-5d81-a7cc-78f1b155f72f" :question/answer-fields Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "22be6cf5-7a6e-540f-98f4-cbe304eff18a" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=2 x$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2.
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 2 \csc^{2}{\left(2 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int \csc^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \csc^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=- \cot{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Integrate with respect to $u$:

$$
\int \csc^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=- \cot{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$

$$"] [:db/add "22be6cf5-7a6e-540f-98f4-cbe304eff18a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "22be6cf5-7a6e-540f-98f4-cbe304eff18a" :question/answer-fields $$

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4.
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \sec^{2}{\left(4 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \sec^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \sec^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=\tan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Integrate with respect to $u$:

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \sec^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{\tan{\left(u \right)}}{4}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{\tan{\left(4 x \right)}}{4}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "5d23c6ec-b347-5bbf-9f87-ded6cedba21a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "5d23c6ec-b347-5bbf-9f87-ded6cedba21a" :question/answer-fields question.:question/problem:
Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \tan{\left(4 x \right)} \sec{\left(4 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=4 x$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4.
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \tan{\left(4 x \right)} \sec{\left(4 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \tan{\left(u \right)} \sec{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \tan{\left(u \right)} \sec{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=\sec{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Integrate with respect to $u$:

$$
\frac{1}{4}\left(\int \tan{\left(u \right)} \sec{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{\sec{\left(u \right)}}{4}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{\sec{\left(4 x \right)}}{4}+C.
$$

Transform both bounds:

\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\pi}{12}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{6}\\x=\frac{\pi}{4}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{\pi}{12}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} 4 \cot{\left(2 x \right)} \csc{\left(2 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cot{\left(u \right)} \csc{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\int \cot{\left(u \right)} \csc{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=- \csc{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Endpoint values: $\csc{\left(\frac{\pi}{6} \right)}=2,\quad \csc{\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \right)}=1$.

Integrate and evaluate:

$$
\left[- 2 \csc{\left(u \right)}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}=\left(-2\right)-\left(-4\right).
$$

The answer is

2.
